skill.description: Run Python workloads through the inference.sh sandbox for data analysis, scraping, media processing, document generation, API access, and automation.
skill.summary: Run Python scripts in a hosted CPU sandbox with common data, web, media, and document libraries.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, or inline library names. Real risks remain: the skill runs belt and npx commands, submits generated Python to a hosted service, permits outbound HTTP in examples, and grants a broad Bash(belt *) tool scope.

remediation.issue: Python source and embedded data are submitted to a third-party execution service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before submission and warn users not to include credentials, private data, or proprietary source.

remediation.issue: The allowed Bash scope permits every belt subcommand.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict the tool permission to the required app-run operation, or use a reviewed wrapper that validates the app identifier and arguments.

remediation.issue: The installation examples execute unpinned npx packages.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions or immutable revisions and document verification steps before execution.

remediation.issue: Example workloads can make unrestricted outbound HTTP requests.
remediation.suggestion: Require destination review, reject sensitive headers by default, and use allowlists where the execution service supports them.

content.user_title: Run Python Tasks in a Hosted Sandbox
content.value_statement: Local environments may lack the libraries or resources required for Python tasks. This skill sends workloads to a hosted CPU sandbox with common packages.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python 3.10 code through the infsh/python-executor application.
Supports execution timeouts from 1 to 300 seconds.
Provides common libraries for data, web, image, video, audio, 3D, and document tasks.
Returns files written to the outputs directory.
Offers default 8 GB and high-memory 16 GB CPU variants.
limitations: Execution requires the belt CLI, an authenticated inference.sh account, and network access.
The environment is CPU-only and does not provide GPU machine-learning libraries.
Workloads are non-interactive, so charts and media must be saved as files.
Code and embedded data are processed by a third-party hosted service.

use_cases.title: Analyze Business Data
use_cases.description: Clean tabular data, calculate summaries, create charts, and return reusable CSV or image files.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate or transform images, videos, audio, PDFs, and 3D models with installed Python libraries.

use_cases.title: Automate Public Data Tasks
use_cases.description: Call approved APIs, parse public web pages, and format results without configuring a local Python environment.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Simple Statistics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to calculate summary statistics for these values: {values}. Return a short table and explain any outliers.

prompt_templates.title: Clean and Chart Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor with pandas to analyze {dataset_description}. Save cleaned data to outputs/cleaned.csv and a chart to outputs/chart.png.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate data analysis with returned files

prompt_templates.title: Extract Public Web Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch {public_url}, parse {fields}, and return a CSV. Respect access rules and do not send credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced network task with an approved public source

prompt_templates.title: Run a High-Memory Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the high-memory python-executor variant for {task}. Validate inputs, set an appropriate timeout, save artifacts under outputs, and summarize verification results.

output_examples.input: Summarize monthly sales and create a bar chart.
output_examples.output: The response reports totals and averages, identifies the strongest month, and returns a chart image.

output_examples.input: Resize an image and convert it to PNG.
output_examples.output: The response confirms the final dimensions and returns the converted PNG file.

output_examples.input: Create a sphere model and report its geometry.
output_examples.output: The response reports vertex and face counts and returns an STL model file.

best_practices: Review generated Python and external destinations before approving execution.
Use explicit timeouts and choose the high-memory variant only when the workload requires it.
Write every required artifact under outputs and verify file contents before presenting results.
anti_patterns: Do not submit secrets, private datasets, or proprietary source without authorization.
Do not use the sandbox for interactive applications or GPU-dependent workloads.
Do not scrape restricted sites or call unapproved endpoints.

faq.question: Does this run Python on my local machine?
faq.answer: No. The belt CLI submits the workload to the hosted infsh/python-executor application.

faq.question: Can it create downloadable files?
faq.answer: Yes. Files saved under outputs are detected and returned with the execution result.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: The examples use outbound HTTP requests. Review every destination and never include credentials without authorization.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The documented variants are CPU-only.

faq.question: What are the execution limits?
faq.answer: Timeouts range from 1 to 300 seconds. The documented memory options are 8 GB and 16 GB.
